chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Musa narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Yazid, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The reward for goodness (al-birr) is hastened, and the punishment for injustice (al-baghy) is hastened. And it is sufficient as a flaw for a man that he looks at people for what is blind to him in himself, and reproaches people for what he cannot leave, and harms his companion with what does not concern him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three main character flaws mentioned in this hadith regarding social interaction?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* underscores the immediacy of divine retribution for *bagh* (transgression) while offering a nuanced critique of human hypocrisy through three specific behavioral flaws. It aligns with the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and self-reflection, warning against projecting one's own inherent weaknesses onto others while neglecting personal accountability. The narration serves as a practical guide for social conduct, linking internal moral integrity with external interactions.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “

The reward of good done to someone is rewarded earlier than other good deeds and an injustice done to someone is punished earlier than other bad deeds. It is enough for one to have the bad quality of peeping   into   confidential   matters   of   other   people,   to continue criticizing others for defects he himself has and to trouble people with senseless talks.”
